source: Fernandez Domingos & Han (2026), 'Falling Behind Drives Unsafe Development in an Idealised AI Race Experiment' (arXiv:2607.26034v1) -- Table 1 (cluster-robust logistic regression, model 6), Table S3 (pairwise treatment contrasts and summary statistics), and main-text Results.
human_sample: N=2,888 participant-round observations (round t>=2, covariate-complete analysed sample), 338 participants, 172 pair clusters. Per-treatment participant counts: p_max=0.1 n=97, p_max=0.6 n=105, p_max=0.9 n=136.
notes: Effects are frozen before any LLM output is inspected, per docs/llm-behavior-analysis-plan.md WS3 T3.4. E4 and E5 are human null results and must be scored by TOST equivalence to zero, never by a failure to reject. E6 is deliberately taken from Table S3 (Cohen's d=0.341, Unsafe HIGHER at the low-risk treatment), not from the Figure 2A caption text, which states the opposite direction for the 0.1-vs-0.6 comparison.

effects.name: opponent_prev_unsafe
effects.description: Model 6 (paper Table 1): the probability of choosing Unsafe increases when the opponent chose Unsafe in the previous round (beta=0.607, SE=0.192, p=0.002).

effects.name: progress_gap_before
effects.description: Model 6: being further ahead (own progress minus opponent progress) reduces the probability of choosing Unsafe (beta=-0.296, SE=0.149, p=0.048).

effects.name: first_round_unsafe
effects.description: Model 6: choosing Unsafe in round 1 predicts later Unsafe play, significant only at the 10% level (beta=0.217, SE=0.116, p<0.10).

effects.name: own_prev_unsafe
effects.description: Model 6: the participant's own previous action is not a robust predictor once the opponent's previous action and race state are included (beta=-0.193, SE=0.192, not significant). This is a null replication and must be scored by TOST equivalence to zero, not by failing to reject.

effects.name: contrast_0.6_vs_0.9
effects.description: Pre-registered 0.6-vs-0.9 contrast on participant-level mean Unsafe frequency: negligible observed effect (Cohen's d=-0.027, t=-0.206, p=0.837, Table S3). This is a null replication and must be scored by equivalence, not by failing to reject.

effects.name: contrast_0.1_vs_0.6
effects.description: 0.1-vs-0.6 contrast on participant-level mean Unsafe frequency (Table S3): Cohen's d=0.341, i.e. Unsafe is HIGHER at the low-risk treatment. Taken from the table value, not the Figure 2A caption, which states the opposite direction.

effects.name: phi_U_overall
effects.description: Overall mean Unsafe frequency (phi_U) across all treatments and rounds (Table S3): 0.584.

effects.name: share_AS
effects.description: Always Safe is never a Nash equilibrium of the reduced four-strategy game at any studied maximum private risk (paper Results/SI) and is not reported as a materially used strategy. No exact participant-level share is given in the main text, so this is a qualitative near-absence anchor rather than a precise observed frequency.
